turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Hi, I'm just going to get you settled and grab some vitals before the doctor comes in. What brings you in today?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh gosh, okay, so my cousin's wedding was Friday, beautiful outdoor thing, though the venue doesn't matter. The dinner is the problem, and then Saturday I started throwing up and I've had diarrhea ever since, and I almost didn't come because I had a client deck due, but I can't be more than ten feet from a bathroom, so.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry you're dealing with that. Let me get the blood pressure, arm out for me.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Sure. I wore this cardigan because the waiting room is always freezing, which is a whole other thing. Is it high? I get nervous in these places.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure is one thirty over eighty... hang on, the cuff shifted. Let me do it again. One eighteen over seventy four.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, that second one sounds more like me. I usually run on the low side, um, when I'm not worked up.

[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Pulse is ninety eight, temperature thirty seven point eight Celsius, oxygen ninety eight percent, and respirations sixteen. You're a little warm and the pulse is up a bit, so I'll tell the doctor.

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Thirty seven point eight, is that a fever? I felt hot Saturday night under the hotel duvet, but I never actually took my temperature, I left the thermometer at home like an idiot.
[SEG0009] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doctor will go over it with you. She's just finishing a note, she'll be right in.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Dr. Shah. I saw the vitals, thanks. So you've had vomiting and diarrhea since the weekend?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, and I want to explain it properly because I think the food did it. Friday was the wedding dinner, not the rehearsal, and they served this seafood pasta, shrimp and scallops in a cream sauce, and I had two plates because I skipped lunch, which was dumb, plus a slice of the lemon cake, and then the speeches went on forever.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Got it, seafood pasta at the wedding. When did the vomiting actually start?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I was going to say it's been five days, but that's wrong, the wedding was Friday and today is Tuesday, and the symptoms didn't start at the wedding, they started Saturday, so three days. The exact hour I can't tell you, I woke up sometime in the night, could've been midnight, could've been four, I just remember the bathroom tile was freezing.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Three days then, since Saturday, time of night unclear. Are you still vomiting?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Saturday was the worst, I threw up, I don't know, four times, maybe five, I stopped counting, and Sunday twice, and then...
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): And since then?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing since yesterday morning. Just waves of nausea if I smell coffee, which is tragic because I live on coffee, I'm a graphic designer and the rebrand deadline is Thursday and my brain is mush without it.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nausea still there, vomiting stopped yesterday morning. What about the diarrhea, how many times are we talking?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh I tried to count. Yesterday I thought it was every hour, like eight or nine, but then I realized I was counting times I went and nothing much happened, so maybe six or seven real ones, watery, just brown water basically, and today I've already gone three times before noon and it's not even... well it's lunchtime-ish now.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): So loosely around six or seven watery stools yesterday, a few already today. Any blood, or black stools?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): The shrimp were kind of pink still, I even said to my sister Elena, are these cooked all the way, and she said the chef knows, and then Elena texted me Sunday that she was sick too, and my cousin's husband, and one of the bridesmaids who had the same pasta, so that's at least three other people, not counting whoever didn't text me back.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's helpful, others from the meal are sick. I did ask about blood though.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Right, sorry, no blood, and not black, nothing tarry, just watery.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Any blood when you were vomiting?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No, it was just the pasta coming back, then yellow stuff. Sorry, that's gross.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): It's fine. Pain in the belly?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Crampy, low down, comes in waves right before I have to go. Not the kind of pain where I can't stand up. More like bad period cramps, but I'm not... well I don't think that's relevant, my period isn't due.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Crampy, not severe. How are you doing with fluids, and are you peeing?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm thirsty all the time and my mouth feels like sandpaper. Pee is darker and I'm going way less, maybe twice yesterday, small amounts. I get woozy if I stand up fast, like the room tilts for a second, then it's okay. I can keep down little sips of water now, ginger ale earlier made it worse so I stopped that.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thirsty, dry mouth, less urine, lightheaded when you stand, but sips of water are staying down. Did you take anything for it?

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): So yes, and I know I wasn't supposed to, the nurse line on Sunday said don't take Imodium if a bunch of you got sick off the same food, but I had a client call Monday and I took it anyway. I thought the dose was twenty milligrams, which is ridiculous, no, it's two milligrams a capsule, and I took two capsules yesterday afternoon. I was about to say I did the same this morning, but I only took one capsule this morning.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Two milligrams a capsule, two of them yesterday, one this morning, even though the nurse line said not to. Anything else, regular medicines?

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Levothyroxine every morning for my thyroid, and the chart might still say seventy five micrograms, but they changed it. It's eighty eight, wait, yes the old dose was seventy five and the bottle I have now is eighty eight micrograms. Except this weekend I'm not a hundred percent sure I took Saturday's, the hotel morning was chaos, though Sunday I think I did and Monday and today I did.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): I do have seventy five micrograms in the chart. We won't sort the exact dose today, just keep taking whatever's on your current bottle. Any other pills, even over the counter?

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister handed me this pink liquid for my stomach at the hotel, I swallowed some Sunday. I want to say Pepto-Bismol, but the bottle was her travel one and the label was rubbed off, so I honestly don't know what it was. I didn't take any more.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Unknown pink liquid, one swallow Sunday, we'll leave that unnamed. Let me take a look at you.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mouth's a bit dry, tongue too. Belly is soft. Tender across the lower abdomen when I press, no guarding, and you're not jumping off the table. Pulse I already saw is up a little, which fits with being a bit dry.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that bad? I read online about kidneys shutting down and I spiraled at two in the morning, which I know is not a medical source, my friend even texted me to stop googling.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't call this kidneys shutting down. What I'm seeing is a stomach bug, most likely from that wedding meal, what I'd call acute gastroenteritis, and on top of it mild dehydration. With several guests sick it could be norovirus, or something bacterial from the seafood. I can't tell those apart just from talking.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): So I don't need, like, a scan or anything? My uncle had his gallbladder out and he started with belly pain, and I keep thinking about that in the middle of the night.

[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): This pattern, vomiting first then watery diarrhea and other people from the same dinner, doesn't sound like a gallbladder attack. No scan today, and I'd like you to stop the loperamide and let the diarrhea run. Fluids are the main treatment, small sips often, an oral rehydration solution if you can get it, Pedialyte or the store brand, not just ginger ale.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Pedialyte, okay. How much? I always overdo it and then I'm sloshing around.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): A few sips every few minutes, not a full glass at once. If a sip comes back up, wait twenty minutes and try again. Eat plain food when you feel up to it, toast, rice, bananas, nothing greasy for a couple of days. Wash your hands well so you don't pass it on, especially with that deadline and other people around.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): The team is remote mostly, but my partner is home, so I'll be careful. What if it just keeps going?
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the diarrhea hasn't settled in three days, or sooner if you see blood, we'll send a stool sample to look for bacteria. I'm not ordering it today.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. And do I come back, or just call, or...

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): If you're not better in three days, come back and we'll do that stool test and recheck you. Sooner, same day, if you can't keep fluids down, you're peeing very little, you get faint rather than just a second of wooziness, there's blood, or a real fever. That's the emergency room, not waiting on me.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Faint, blood, can't keep fluids, got it. The thyroid pill, do I still take it if I'm queasy?

[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, take the levothyroxine as on your bottle, with a sip of water, away from the calcium in any rehydration drink by a few hours if you can. We still have seventy five in the chart and you're saying eighty eight, so bring the bottle next time and we'll fix the record. I don't want to guess.

[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll put the bottle in my bag tonight so I don't forget. I do that thing where I leave it by the coffee maker and then walk out without it. Thank you, I feel less like I'm dying.
[SEG0051] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can walk you out whenever you're ready, and I'll print the after-visit note. No labs going out from us today unless the doctor added one.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nothing today. Stool only if she meets what we just said. Thanks.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): One more thing, the lightheaded part, is it okay to drive? The clinic lot is kind of far from the door and my car's an old stick shift.

[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): If you feel steady sitting here now, a short drive is reasonable. If the room tilts when you stand, sit back down and get a ride. Start the sips before you get in the car.

spec.situation: Diarrhoea and vomiting after a trip or a wedding meal; others at the event are ill; patient counts bowel movements loosely; takes loperamide against advice; mild dehydration signs; stool test conditional; advice on fluids.
features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

bad.reason: Dose/timing supported, but status not current; doctor told patient to stop loperamide.
bad.text: loperamide (dose=2 mg, frequency=2 capsules yesterday afternoon and 1 capsule this morning, indication=diarrhea, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: No rebound tenderness not explicitly stated; 'not jumping off the table' is not clear rebound exam.

omissions.text: History supportive of foodborne outbreak: at least three other wedding attendees who ate the same pasta were also sick, including the patient's sister Elena, the cousin's husband, and a bridesmaid.
Patient reported being able to keep down small sips of water now, and that ginger ale made symptoms worse so she stopped it.
Levothyroxine dose is incompletely recorded: patient said the current bottle is 88 micrograms and the chart still lists 75 micrograms.
No labs or other tests were ordered today; stool testing was explicitly deferred unless symptoms persist/worsen as discussed.
